Thanks again for the catch-up last week. As promised, attached is a short usage snapshot for the last 90 days (attachment: 20251101-acme-usage-report.csv). A couple of quick notes from our side: 

- Token spend increased ~38% month-over-month driven by the new product search feature (peak 850k tokens/day).
- Average 95th percentile latency on the current plan is holding at ~180ms, but we’re seeing occasional spikes during bulk inference windows.
- Your existing committed capacity will start to feel constrained if the current growth continues — we estimate a need for ~20–25% additional reserved throughput to avoid throttling during peak hours.

Given that your renewal is coming up in mid-November, I wanted to propose a short call to review: 1) a modest capacity uplift (20%) on Dedicated for Q1, 2) a term amendment that staggers the commitment to match forecasted growth, and 3) a small one-time credit to cover overages from the last two months while you transition.

If that sounds reasonable I can loop finance with a draft amendment and a capacity/pricing table. Availability: I have 30-minute slots Mon/Tue next week between 9–12 PT.

Thanks,
Sergio

Elena, Jared — thanks for the quick reply. I pulled together a concise proposal and attached a redlineable amendment (attachment: 20251104-acme-proposal-v2.pdf). Summary below: 

- Recommended change: increase Dedicated reserved capacity by 20% (from 5 units -> 6 units equivalent) starting 2026-01-01.
- Pricing: list price + 12% uplift for the additional capacity (pro-rated for remainder of current term if we execute before 2025-12-01). Example line items included in the PDF.
- One-time credit: Redwood will apply a $12,000 billing credit to offset historical overage charges for Sep–Oct 2025, contingent on executing the amendment by 2025-11-15.
- Term amendment: propose keeping the current 12-month term but allow a scheduled capacity review at month 6 to re-evaluate commitments (no penalty for moving up capacity if both parties agree).
- Ops changes: no new VPC subnets required. We’ll just update the routing policy to include the extra capacity; IP allowlist will remain the same. We will schedule a maintenance window (low traffic) for the rollout.

If that aligns, we can: 1) lock in pricing and pro-rate through your current billing cycle, 2) have Procurement sign the amendment and 3) schedule a short rollout window with Ops. 

Proposed 30-minute call times this week: Wed 11/5 10:00 PT or Thu 11/6 11:00 PT. 

Best,
